finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches a URL taken directly from the query string and returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the response body. An attacker can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, or localhost, and read the response. This is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, with the response body returned at app.py:17

trace.note: Route /preview is registered with no authentication
requests.get(target) is called with no scheme, host or IP validation, and follows redirects by default
resp.text[:500] and the status code are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No validation on this path. There is no allowlist, no scheme check, no private or loopback IP blocking, and no redirect restriction. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check is applied only in /partner, not here.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the `url` query parameter and passes it unvalidated to requests.get at app.py:16, and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 characters of the body; the ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:24 applies only to /partner, and app.py is the only file, so no middleware exists.
